paragraphs: Friend, this passage is heavy, so I'm going to say it plain. Judas was filled with remorse, and he said, "I have sinned by betraying innocent blood" (Matthew 27:3-4). Feeling awful about what you did and telling the truth about it is a real start. But in this passage, he carries it to men who answer, "What is that to us?" and "You bear the responsibility" (Matthew 27:4).

Now look at who he took it to. The chief priests and elders had just spent the morning plotting to put Jesus to death (Matthew 27:1), and then they said the silver couldn't go into the treasury because it was blood money, and bought a field with it (Matthew 27:6-7). Friend, I think it's possible to be very careful about the small rules and still walk right past the big thing. I've seen bakers who'd check the oven timer three times and never smell the smoke.

Here's what I want you to carry out of this one: Matthew points back to the prophet's words about the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Jesus by the people of Israel, and says they were fulfilled. Those words end with "as the Lord had commanded me," so even on this dark morning, I think Jesus is not out of God's story (Matthew 27:9-10). When your own mess feels too big, don't hand it to people who say "You bear the responsibility." Bring it to Jesus, friend, and stay close, because this story is far from over.
